observations: Photo 0 shows a pile of green corded drills, many with Bosch branding, mixed in with other tools.
Photo 1 shows a close-up of a green Bosch drill with 'BOSCH' and 'BIT CORE PLUS' visible on the side.
The drills appear used, with visible wear, scratches, and some damage on the body and cord.
The seller claims it is a 'Bosch drilling machine' and '220v 13mm', but no photo shows the plug or the drill bit size.
The cord is coiled and appears to be standard 3-pin, not 13mm as claimed.

claims.evidence: The brand 'Bosch' is visible in both photos, but the voltage '220v' and bit size '13mm' are not visible on any label or part. The cord appears to be standard 3-pin, not 13mm.

risks.risk: The drill may not be 220v as claimed, or may not be compatible with Nigerian 220v power supply.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the power plug and any voltage label on the drill.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working or incompatible

risks.risk: The drill may not have a 13mm bit size, or the bit may be missing or damaged.
risks.proof: A photo showing the drill bit attached to the chuck, or a close-up of the chuck and bit size.
risks.if_unproven: priced as missing or damaged bit

risks.risk: The drill may be damaged or non-functional due to visible wear and tear.
risks.proof: A video or photo showing the drill in operation, or a close-up of the motor and internal components.

proof_requests: Close-up of the label with the model number, usually on the side or back near the motor.
A clear photo of the power plug and any voltage label on the drill.
A photo showing the drill bit attached to the chuck, or a close-up of the chuck and bit size.
A video or photo showing the drill in operation.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
